name: HEY
tagline: Opinionated paid email service with screening, bundles, and privacy defaults

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; 4+ character personal address is $99/year, equivalent to $8.25/month.

tiers.name: HEY for Families
tiers.limits: Up to 5 people total (account holder + 4 additional people), each with a separate @hey.com address and account.

tiers.name: HEY for Domains
tiers.limits: Custom-domain email with central billing; first user is $10/month and each additional user is $12/month.
tiers.notes: Monthly only; no annual plan and no free trial.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; HEY for You and Families have a 30-day trial, while HEY for Domains has no free trial
pricing.billingTerms: HEY for You and Families are annual only; HEY for Domains is monthly only; prices are USD and taxes may be added
pricing.hiddenCosts: Ultra-short @hey.com addresses cost extra each year: $999/year for 2 characters and $349/year for 3 characters; 4+ characters are included with the normal personal plan.

verdictSummary: You can build an email client, but replacing HEY means running a trustworthy email service: deliverability, spam filtering, abuse handling, storage, mobile apps, and reputation.
coreLoopDIY: Build a personal mail client on top of IMAP/SMTP or a hosted mailbox; do not try to replace the global email service layer casually.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because email is infrastructure; deliverability and trust are the product.

priorArt.name: Mail-in-a-Box
priorArt.desc: Open-source personal mail server stack; useful prior art but deliverability remains the mo

notes: Valuable no: the UI is cloneable, but email infrastructure is not an afternoon project.
prompt:
Build me an email client with HEY's screening and bundling ideas, running on
top of a mailbox I already pay for (Fastmail, Gmail, anything with IMAP).
Requirements:

- A local web app: Node + Express + better-sqlite3, binds to localhost;
  imapflow for reading, nodemailer for sending, creds in .env.
- The screener: mail from first-time senders lands in a screening view where I
  approve or block; decisions persist in SQLite and apply to all future mail.
- Bundles: approved senders get a category; newsletters render in a batched
  feed view, receipts in a paper-trail list; only approved humans hit the
  inbox.
- Reply-later: mark a thread and it sits in a persistent to-answer stack until
  cleared.
- Write decisions back as IMAP folders and labels so my phone's mail app
  roughly mirrors the sorting.
- Strip remote images in the reading pane by default.
- No accounts of its own, no telemetry; mail stays at my provider.
- Out of scope: running an SMTP server, custom domains, and mobile apps. Do not
  replace the mail service itself; deliverability and spam reputation are the
  product and cannot be rebuilt solo.
- README: per-provider app-password setup, and a warning that Gmail OAuth is a
  project of its own, use an app password or Fastmail to keep this a weekend.
